title: Engine skeleton: daemon + SQLite v2 state + CLI projection read
goal: Stand up the minimal durable core of STC v2: a Tokio daemon whose only source of truth is a greenfield SQLite v2 database (WAL, single-writer discipline), plus studio-cli read verbs that are pure projections of that DB. Crash-anytime-safe: SIGKILL mid-write leaves the DB consistent and recovery idempotent. No UI.
acceptance: studio status exits 0 reading real DB (no mock)
50x kill -9 leaves 0 corrupt rows + 0 orphaned worktrees
ported modules cite v1 sha256 + pass tests/clippy in v2
brief: Create branch v2-greenfield off main; archive v1 (.factory/.roadmap/.research/.fallow) to .archive/v1 then clear. Scaffold workspace studio-core (state, ledger, projection) + studio-cli. Greenfield v2 schema, no v1 migration. Port {state,ledger,projection,worktree} ONLY if tests pass + clippy clean in the v2 tree; else rewrite. Enforce single-writer discipline (VERIFIED: one write txn at a time) and CHECKPOINT the WAL to avoid unbounded growth (VERIFIED: WAL grows without bound under continuous readers). Be careful with POSIX advisory locks across fd close (VERIFIED). studio status must work WITHOUT a live daemon.
verdict: pass — CLOSED (dual QA pass, rounds 7+8). Pending explicit user sign-off per loop gate.

evidence.note: alpha_completed=false -> its internal claims are HYPOTHESIS unless re-verified below

evidence.claim: SQLite rolls back partial transactions after crash/power failure
evidence.quote: If an application crash, or an operating-system crash, or even a power failure occurs in the middle of a transaction, the partially written transaction should be automatically rolled back the next time the database file is accessed.

evidence.claim: close() cancels POSIX advisory locks for the whole process (fatal for multi-fd worktree lock hygiene)
evidence.quote: One particularly pernicious problem is that the close() system call will cancel all POSIX advisory locks on the same file for all threads and all file descriptors in the process.

evidence.claim: SQLite permits many concurrent readers but exactly one writer
evidence.quote: SQLite supports multiple simultaneous read transactions coming from separate database connections, possibly in separate threads or processes, but only one simultaneous write transaction.

evidence.claim: WAL grows without bound if readers never release (checkpoint starvation)
evidence.quote: if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

evidence.claim: SQLite FS writes amplify disk use (~20% over db size)
evidence.quote: the database file will be 1,024,512,000 bytes in size and the test1.dir directory will use 1,228,800,000 bytes of space (according to "du -k"), about 20% more than the database.

open_blockers.severity: LOW (non-blocking; dead code on target kernel)

open_blockers.status: PARTIALLY FIXED — forged-row vector closed (QA-A r6), but binding defeated by DB copy (see A-DB-COPY-01)
open_blockers.defect: The `own_abandoned` exemption unlocks+reaps any path named in a `creating` row of the RUNNING engine's ledger, with zero ownership check. A second engine (same repo/root) forges `INSERT INTO worktrees VALUES('<victim-live>','<same repo>','forged','creating',…)` into its OWN dbB, runs `gc`, and destroys the first engine's live locked worktree: `reaped_creating` + `reaped_git_orphans` contain it, dir + admin entry gone, exit 0. Re-opens the exact B(ii) class the fix closed. (Different-repo variant held — hole is precisely the same-repo model.)
open_blockers.required_fix: exemption must prove ownership (e.g. creator token written into the worktree at creation and matched at reap; or equivalent) — never trust ledger content alone.

open_blockers.class: porcelain parse bypass → deletion while reporting refusal
open_blockers.status: FIXED & QA-VERIFIED (QA-A r6 + QA-B r6 attack B held incl. fallback, CR/TAB/unicode/long)
open_blockers.defect: `git worktree add "$ROOT/evil<LF>locked"` succeeds (git allows newlines). `parse_worktree_porcelain` splits on lines and matches `== "locked"`, recording a truncated PHANTOM path. One `gc`: `refused_locked` names the phantom while `swept_dirs` includes the REAL newline path's `.git` — the entire registered worktree is deleted while the report claims refusal, exit 0.
open_blockers.required_fix: harden the parse (porcelain -z / NUL-delimited if available, else reject any path containing control characters) — refuse to manage newline-bearing paths, never reap them; exact-match must cover the real path.

open_blockers.status: RECORDED — operator story + gc exit code in scope of third waiver
open_blockers.defect: N abandoned git-locked worktrees with no ledger row are refused forever (only `own_abandoned` unlocks, which needs a row). Manual `git worktree unlock` works. Fail-closed for safety, never-self-healing. Also: `gc` exits 0 while reporting `clean:false` + refusals (exit-code gap).

open_blockers.class: identity binding defeated by normal operator action
open_blockers.status: PARTIALLY FIXED — copy-after-migration diverges (QA-A r7), but pre-fix-shape copies share the id (see D-MIGRATION-01)
open_blockers.defect: `cp studio.db backup.db` clones `engine_meta`, so two engines share one engine_id. The copy + forged creating row + same repo/root reaps the victim (`reaped_creating` + `reaped_git_orphans`, dir + admin gone, forged row consumed, gc_exit=1). `init` on the copy keeps the cloned id (NOT regenerated). Backup/restore/cp is a normal operator action — the ownership proof is silently voided by it.
open_blockers.required_fix: bind engine identity beyond the DB file (e.g. store (st_dev,st_ino) at init; regenerate engine_id when the live file identity differs), so a copy diverges on first open while the original keeps its id.

open_blockers.status: FIXED & QA-VERIFIED (QA-A r7: unlock-then-gc still refused; release recourse; per-DB; help documents the story)
open_blockers.defect: Refused forged rows linger forever (no CLI clears them; only hand sqlite DELETE). The documented remedy (`git worktree unlock` then `gc`) causes gc to REAP the foreign worktree (dir gone, admin gone, verify flips clean). Attacker plants the row; operator following --help destroys the victim. Receipt discloses lingering but not the trap.
open_blockers.required_fix: persist refused paths per DB (once refused, never auto-reaped) + an explicit operator release command; unlocking must not re-arm auto-reap of a refused path.

open_blockers.class: migration keep-and-bind preserves a shared id
open_blockers.status: FIXED & QA-VERIFIED (QA-A r8 + QA-B r8: half-pair, races, in-place writes, keep-cases all held)
open_blockers.defect: A DB in pre-fix shape (engine_id, no dev/ino) copied BEFORE first post-fix open: both files keep-and-bind the SAME id (orig binds orig ino, copy binds copy ino — id shared). Forged-row kill chain via the copy reaps the victim (dir + marker gone, shared id in report). Worse than legacy: an attacker can MANUFACTURE pre-fix shape with one sqlite DELETE of the pair, so this is reachable, not historical.
open_blockers.required_fix: regenerate (never keep) when no stored pair exists. Safe because: current-binary init writes id+pair atomically, so 'no pair' implies 'created by an older binary', and older binaries never issued studio:<id> lock reasons — nothing live can reference the discarded id. Verify the atomicity; add a regression test (pre-fix-shape copy → divergent ids, victim refused). Also correct the receipt/docs in-place-overwrite claim (reality diverges — safer than documented).
